ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows circle V with center V. Segment QS passes horizontally through V, so Q and S are opposite endpoints of a diameter. Radii are drawn from V to Q, R, S, T, and P. The angle between VR and VS is marked as a right angle. The central angle between VS and VT is labeled 75°, and the central angle between VT and VP is labeled 72°. Reasoning: Since QS is a diameter, each semicircle from Q to S measures 180°. The lower semicircle consists of arcs QP, PT, and TS. Arc PT = 72° and arc TS = 75°, so arc QP = 180° - 72° - 75° = 33°. The upper semicircle consists of arcs QR and RS. Since angle RVS is 90°, arc RS = 90°, so arc QR = 180° - 90° = 90°. The requested arc PQR is arc PQ plus arc QR, so m arc PQR = 33° + 90° = 123°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at V with radii drawn to Q, R, S, T, and P. From the image, note that ∠RVS is marked as a right angle, so arc RS is 90°, ∠SVT is 75°, and ∠TVP is 72°. From the text, use that QS is a diameter, so each semicircle from Q to S has measure 180°. On the lower semicircle, arc QP + arc PT + arc TS = 180°, so arc QP = 180 - 72 - 75 = 33°. On the upper semicircle, arc QR + arc RS = 180°, so arc QR = 180 - 90 = 90°. The requested arc PQR is arc PQ plus arc QR, giving 33 + 90 = 123.
